standard.title: Construct representations with intention
standard.description: experiment with ways to construct representations that reflect ideas, perspectives and/or meaning, and/or use of media conventions, media languages and media technologies
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can manipulate media languages to change meaning and develop production skills across multiple forms. They can apply genre conventions deliberately. They have not yet experimented systematically with how an auteur, genre or film movement shapes a distinctive representational language — or used target audience research to inform production.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students experiment with ways to construct representations that reflect ideas, perspectives and/or meaning using media conventions, languages and technologies — informed by analysis of practitioners and target audience research.

nodes.label: Auteur, genre and representational language
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can analyse how a specific media artist (auteur, social media influencer, game designer, music video director) uses technical and symbolic codes to construct a recognisable representational language — and apply this analysis to inform their own construction experiments.
nodes.minimum_width: Analyse how one media artist uses at least three technical and symbolic elements to construct a distinctive representational language, and apply one observed technique in an original production experiment.
nodes.typical_width: Examine how auteurs, genre directors, social media influencers and game designers use technical and symbolic codes to construct representations; apply findings to design and production experiments; investigate multiple practitioners and identify common and divergent approaches.
wider: Investigate a specific auteur or film movement's use of mise-en-scène, camera work, sound and editing to construct a recognisable visual language — produce an original work that pays homage to or responds to that language, documenting the design decisions

Research how a social media influencer or game designer uses technical and symbolic elements to construct audience relationships — apply findings to produce an original media arts work that builds a specific audience relationship using the same strategies
nodes.hinge_reason: Auteur/practitioner analysis is the conceptual foundation for informed experimentation — without it, production experiments are undirected, and the connection between technical choices and representational intent cannot be articulated.

response_modes.reason: Use Viewpoints questions to build the analysis-to-production reasoning chain: 'How does this director's use of sound construct the audience relationship? How could I apply or subvert this in my own work?'

success_criteria: Student can analyse how a media artist uses at least three technical and symbolic elements to construct a distinctive representational language
Student can apply at least one observed technique in original production work with a documented rationale

nodes.label: Audience research and production experimentation
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can research a target audience and use findings to design and produce a media arts work — experimenting with multiple production approaches and selecting the most effective for the intended audience relationship.
nodes.minimum_width: Research a target audience for a planned media arts work (identifying genre, platform, and representative media conventions for that audience) and use at least two findings to shape production decisions.
nodes.typical_width: Research target audiences and conventions in successful online media arts works; use research to inform design, production and post-production decisions; manipulate technical and symbolic codes to produce works for identified target audiences; experiment with multiple production approaches and select the most effective.
wider: Research target audiences and conventions in successful online media arts works — use findings to design and produce a work that deliberately constructs audience relationships, documenting at each production stage how research findings shaped decisions

Manipulate technical and symbolic codes across multiple production drafts for the same target audience — comparing how different approaches position the audience differently, and selecting the final approach with a documented justification

response_modes.reason: Build students' repertoire of production experimentation strategies — multiple drafts, audience comparison, approach selection. The more systematic the experimentation, the more informed the final production decisions.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The range of experimentation approaches at Y9-10 (auteur analysis, audience research, multi-draft production, genre manipulation) is genuinely rich — students who experiment across multiple approaches develop much stronger critical production thinking.
success_criteria: Student researches a target audience and identifies at least two media conventions specific to that audience
Student uses those findings to make and document at least two production decisions
